# The step-5b/5c review — 2026-09-03

**A dated record. Do not edit it.** The decisions it records live in
`prds/prd-Inflozo-2026-08-17/reconcile-designs-decisions.md` §A12; what was fixed afterwards is
recorded in the generators' own docstrings and comments (each patch names its finding id) and in
`build-sequence.md` steps 5b and 5c. This file says what the review found and what the owner ruled.

## Verdict, as delivered

**Not ready to walk yet.** The annotated prototype (5b) was sound as a checking tool and needed only
scaffolding fixes. The walkthrough (5c) would have misled the owner as it stood: its deploy wizard
page rendered blank; roughly a third of its links and triggers were attached to the wrong element;
it printed plan figures the PRD had overruled while its own notes said they were corrected; half its
screens could not be reached by clicking; and the process documents described behaviour — the design
ring, the backup gate, a six-step wizard — that no screen had. **None of the fixes changed the
design.** Every one was in a generator, in the walkthrough's own additions, or in a document. The
frames stayed byte-identical to the export throughout.

Counts as the report stated them that day, kept here because a record may state a count: 10
blockers, 45 majors, 44 minors, 14 notes across 113 merged findings, plus nine round-2 findings; 3
refuted and dropped (F-095, F-101, R2-1); 0 fixes needing a design change to clear a blocker.

## The ten blockers, by id

| id | What was reproduced | Route |
|---|---|---|
| F-001 | 5c's deploy page rendered blank — the lifter stripped the frame's fixed height and the wizard root had nothing else to give it one | `frames.py` (unbox keeps a height) and a build check |
| F-002 | Triggers landed on an icon's closing tag when the matched text followed an icon | `frames.py` element finder; build check that no attribute lands on a closing tag |
| F-003 | The same finder matched text inside an attribute value and wrapped a whole screen in a link to itself | `frames.py`; build check |
| F-005 | Rail links (Projects, Sites, Assets) and Ship it, Connect site, the passkey button did nothing for the same reason | `frames.py`; build check |
| F-006 | `build-sequence.md`, `HANDOVER.md`, `INDEX.md`, the board and `_screens.html` described a 5c with a design ring, a backup gate, a six-step wizard and a full keyboard map; no product screen carried any of those hooks | the documents, rewritten from the build |
| F-007 | Billing, Pricing, Upgrade and Assets printed plan limits Appendix F.1 overrules, while the generator's notes said they were patched | decision 2 |
| F-011 | Following links from Sign In reached about half the screens; the rest were reachable only from the jump list | `build-app.py` wiring of the drawn menu rows; a reachability check |
| F-013 | Drawn screens (Design Picker, Edit Lock, Snapshot Gate, Library Update, Sites on Free) were absent from 5c and its hold-out list said they had never been drawn | `build-app.py` lifts them as overlays; the hold-out list corrected |
| F-014 | The design ring was a one-way hop to a hover picture; the drawn arrows and counter were inert | `build-app.py` steps the ring between its two drawn positions (S4c and S6) with `]`, `[` and the drawn ◀ ▶ and opens the Design Picker sheet; the on-section nav (B1b) stays held out |
| F-041 | The passkey sheet was hand-written in the walkthrough's own vocabulary instead of lifting S1c | `build-app.py` lifts S1c |

## The six decisions

The owner took **option 1 on every one** (2026-09-03).

| # | Decision | Options, as put to him |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | How to get to the walk | **(1) Fix the generators and the documents, then walk both builds — RECOMMENDED, taken.** (2) Walk 5b now and treat 5c as broken. (3) Drop 5c. |
| 2 | The plan figures the frames got wrong (F-007) | **(1) Patch the four strings in 5c to Appendix F.1 at lift time, each patch naming the ruling; A7 fixes the frames — RECOMMENDED, taken.** (2) Leave the frames' figures and put a visible note on those screens. |
| 3 | Which build is the gate, and what "walked it" means (F-084) | **(1) 5b is R-75's gate, exactly as the ruling names it; 5c is walked afterwards for feel. "Walked" means every journey and flow on 5b's front door opened end to end, with the owner's notes in one named file (`ux-designs/WALK-NOTES.md`); the date line in `build-sequence.md` stays his — RECOMMENDED, taken.** (2) Make 5c the gate. |
| 4 | The accessibility fixes that would change the design | **(1) Send them to Claude Design so the export fixes its own frames — RECOMMENDED, taken, with one correction from the owner: they go to prompt A7, not A8, because they correct existing frames.** (2) Fix them in the stylesheet now — an R-74 breach. |
| 5 | The backup gate's download promise (F-077) | **(1) Amend FR-J13: the download is offered when the Staff Access Token is present; otherwise the gate names the Ghost Admin path — RECOMMENDED, taken.** (2) Keep FR-J13 and require the token before any first deploy — contradicts FR-C1. |
| 6 | Frames drawn on the wrong mechanism, shown uncorrected in 5c (F-008) | **(1) Hold them out of 5c until A7 runs, except copy the PRD owns: Redesign Proposals (B22) held out entirely; the Pro Exit Sheet stays and its remedy count is A7's; the Starter Chooser stays and its roster is A7's; S4d's paid-tier rows are A7's — RECOMMENDED, taken.** (2) Patch them structurally in the walkthrough — invents markup beside the export. |

## Where the finding data lives

- **The report the owner read:** the artifact *Before the Walk*, rendered from the reviewing
  session's scratchpad (`before-the-walk.html`). It carries the verdict, the blockers, the decisions
  with their options, the majors and minors grouped by owner, what was checked and found sound, and
  what was refuted.
- **The findings themselves:** the reviewing session's scratchpad, `review/` — `merged.json` (every
  finding with id, where, evidence per reviewer, problem, why it matters, proposed fix),
  `final.json` (the two verifiers' notes per finding: what was reproduced, and the severity and fix
  route), `extras.json` (the round-2 findings, `R2-…`). A scratchpad is session-local and not
  checked in; the ids survive in the generators' comments and in §A12.
- **Method.** Twelve reviewer lenses — Ghost, architecture, implementability, testability, the
  user's walk, accessibility, requirements, document consistency, shipping pragmatics, a stand-in
  for the owner, an R-74 fidelity audit, security — then a completeness critic with two more
  lenses. Every finding was checked by two independent verifiers, one reproducing the evidence by
  execution and one judging severity and whether the fix touches the design. The blockers were
  additionally reproduced in the main session by rendering the pages headless.
- **Not covered.** No Ghost(Pro) server exists, so every Ghost(Pro) claim is cited, not executed.
  No screen reader was run. Firefox could not be driven headless, so keyboard focusability of
  `display:contents` anchors was confirmed in Chromium only. The tablet and 200%-zoom editor layouts
  cannot be checked in either build until prompt A8 draws them.

## What the fixes were routed to

Four agents, one per owning surface: the 5b generator (`prototype/build.py`, `frames.py`), the 5c
generator (`walkthrough/build-app.py`, `app.js`, `_app.css`), the spines and normative documents
(`EXPERIENCE.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `prd.md`, the architecture files, §A12), and the process documents
(`build-sequence.md`, `HANDOVER.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the INDEX briefs, the board). Anything that would
change what a frame looks like went to prompt A7 instead of being applied.
